Collectr.title: Collectr - TCG Collector App
Collectr.desc:
Why use multiple apps when you can track all your TCGs in one place? Most collectors collect multiple TCGs. Whether you are a Pokemon collector, Magic collector, One Piece collector, Lorcana collector, YuGiOh collector, MetaZoo collector, or even a Funko collector, this app is for you!



Collectr is a next-generation portfolio manager. We allow you to manage, track and value all your raw, graded and sealed cards in the palm of your hand. It’s never been easier to view your TCG collections as a portfolio. 



Leverage our real-time database of 1,000,000+ products to instantly value your products. 



We have data available for the following TCGs:
- Magic The Gathering
- Yu-Gi-Oh!
- Pokémon
- One Piece
- Vanguard
- Force of Will
- Weiss Schwarz
- Final Fantasy
- Star Wars Destiny
- Dragon Ball Super
- Dragon Ball Fusion World
- Funko
- Sorcery
- Grand Archive
- Palworld
- Cyberpunk TCG
- Transformers
- Flesh and Blood
- Digimon
- Gate Ruler
- MetaZoo


KEY FEATURES 
- Build Your Collection - Search and add products from our 200,000+ product catalog
- Value Your Portfolio - Instantly understand and track the value of your collections
- Track Market Trends - Gain real-time insights into the performance of your collection
- Multi-Currency Support - Know the value of your collection in any currency (including crypto!)
- Biggest Gains/Losses - Understand the biggest movers in your portfolio in real-time


ADDITIONAL FEATURES THAT REQUIRE IN-APP PURCHASE
- Unlimited Card Scanning
- Exclusive Filters
- Data Exports
- Social Custom Backgrounds

Download our app today and start managing your collection in the most advanced and efficient way possible!

Beware! The only format this app will import is TCGplayer CSV, but it only outputs its own proprietary format. The fact that it can’t even import the file it exports itself is beyond absurd and feels like malicious design to keep you locked into their app and unable to switch to another one. It’s essentially a lie to say that this app even has export functionality when that very export functionality is not compatible with anything, even the app’s own import functionality. I downloaded the app to track my sealed magic collection, which it was doing a wonderful job. That was until I tried to edit my quantities. 

I decided to open one of my products for my personal collection. The app saw this a loss to my overall portfolio, really screwing up the overall number values. I tried adding it as a “sold” product, still showed as a loss. This made NO sense to me. I reached out in their discord and spoke with a moderator who basically told me “That’s too bad bud, that’s not what our app is ment for”. 

I gave him a scenario about what if I scanned a product multiple times by mistake and didn’t want that to reflect a deficit on my portfolios worth. They said I would have to submit a ticket to have the problem fix if able. 

Needless to say I stopped scanning my collection on this app on that day. I since then have found another app that lets me change my inventory quantity without being penalized.

I’ve been using TCG Collector for a week now and honestly, it’s made keeping track of my cards so much easier. The scanner is probably my favorite feature because I don’t have to manually search for every single card. It’s quick, simple, and makes going through a bigger collection way less tedious. I also like being able to see my cards organized in one place instead of trying to remember what I already have. The app is pretty easy to navigate, even when you’re just getting started, and I like that it gives you a better idea of what’s actually in your collection. There are still little things I’d like to see improved, but overall it’s been a really useful app for anyone who collects cards. If you have a growing collection and want an easier way to organize and keep track of everything, I’d definitely recommend giving it a try.

The card scanning feature is also very useful and saves a lot of time when adding cards to my collection.
Another thing I like is being able to see the estimated value of my collection. It makes it easy to keep track of how my collection changes over time. The app also has a clean layout so it doesn’t feel confusing when you are trying to find something.
Overall, Collectr is a great app for anyone who collects trading cards. Whether you have a small collection or a large one, it makes keeping everything organized much easier. I would definitely recommend giving it a try if you collect TCG cards

CollX.title: CollX: Sports Card Scanner
CollX.desc:
CollX (pronounced "collects") answers the question every collector has: "What's it worth?" The app lets you scan virtually any sports, trading card game, or non-sport card! That includes baseball, basketball, football, wrestling, hockey, soccer, MMA, boxing, golf, tennis— as well as TCG cards like Pokemon, Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Flesh & Blood, One Piece, Disney Lorcana, and even Non-Sport categories like Garbage Pail Kids, Marvel, and Star Wars. CollX will instantly identify the card and get the average market value. Once you've scanned your cards, add them to your collection and track your portfolio. You can also buy and sell via the CollX marketplace, where you can purchase cards with a credit card, get shipping and tracking, and earn cash selling your cards to other collectors. Turn the hobby into your side hustle!

COLLX SPORTS AND TCG SCANNER
CollX's visual search technology instantly recognizes and matches against a database of 20+ million cards. After identifying the best match, you'll get the current average market price for the card. Our deep-learning models were created by a team with 10+ years experience developing image recognition technology. In addition to being able to match most RAW cards, CollX will also identify graded cards, as well as parallel and reprint versions of cards.

BUY AND SELL
The CollX marketplace is the fastest growing place to buy and sell cards. Use Deals to bundle multiple cards and make an offer to the Seller. As a Seller, you can utilize several shipping options, including CollX Envelope, where you'll get tracked shipping for as little as $0.75! Other Seller Tools include the ability to set a bulk discount, accept offers, and vacation mode. Cards bought through the CollX marketplace are covered by CollX Protect, where payments are only released when the cards arrive at the Buyer, giving peace of mind to both parties in a deal.

COLLX AI
The first AI built specifically for the trading card hobby, CollX AI provides insights on cards, coaching tips on how to do everything from negotiate to ship, and even can assist in helping sell your cards faster. 

GO PRO
CollX Pro is a monthly subscription tier on CollX offering several power-user features, including:
- Unlimited Collection Size
- $10 Monthly Credit on CollX Marketplace
- Featured Listings
- Access to CollX AI
- EasyPrice (dynamic repricing)
- Export Collection as CSV spreadsheet
- Printable Checklists
And much much more! CollX Pro is $10/month or $100/year.

GET HISTORICAL PRICING
CollX uses millions of historical auction prices to calculate a card's average value. As you add cards to your collection, you'll see your overall portfolio value grow. As your cards rise or fall in value, CollX helps you track both individual card values and your overall portfolio value. No more wondering what your Pokémon card value is!

BUILD YOUR CARD COLLECTION
Create and keep track of your card values. View your collection as a grid, list, or as sets. You can also filter and sort your cards by a variety of criteria — value, date added, year, team, etc. Export as spreadsheet and generate set checklists with CollX Pro. 

SEARCH CARDS
Search 20+ million cards in our database or the millions of CollX user cards for sale. Save your favorite searches to get email, push or in-app notifications when those cards are added for sale. 

When you click on links to various merchants on this site and make a purchase, this can result in this app earning a commission. Affiliate programs include, but are not limited to, the eBay Partner Network.

Read our Terms of Use at https://www.collx.app/terms

I have been a paying Pro member on this platform for multiple years, and while most of my purchases have gone smoothly, my experiences with customer service have been consistently frustrating whenever an issue arises.

When making purchases on a platform of this size, encountering fraudulent sellers or counterfeit cards is an unfortunate reality. What matters is how the platform handles these situations and protects its customers. Unfortunately, resolving these issues has been an unnecessarily exhausting process. Despite supposedly having access to “priority” customer service as a Pro member, I have routinely faced delays spanning multiple days, with responses often limited to a single message per day at best. Resolving even straightforward issues becomes a drawn-out ordeal.

My experience dealing with one particular customer service representative, Tim, has been especially frustrating. Most recently, after a dispute involving counterfeit cards I received, the platform blocked my payment methods entirely. Despite being a paying member for multiple years and maintaining a strong positive rating, I was left unable to use the platform without what appeared to be any meaningful outreach, explanation, or attempt to investigate the underlying issue.

It is incredibly disappointing to be treated this way after years of paid membership and positive transaction history. Rather than feeling that my loyalty is valued or that I have access to better support as a Pro member, I feel penalized for raising a legitimate concern about the authenticity of items I purchased.

A premium membership should come with meaningful customer support, particularly when disputes involving potentially counterfeit products arise. Instead, my experience has been characterized by slow communication, frustrating interactions, and a lack of transparency. Based on these experiences, I find it difficult to justify continuing to pay for a membership that has failed to provide the level of service it advertises.

reviews.t: Customer Service and tracking is trash
reviews.b: The app itself isn’t bad. I enjoy the options to buy and sell and how easy it is to use. However, their tracking system is terrible. You may or may not get updates on where your package is, the tracking number may or may not appear in USPS system as an actual tracking number and sometimes you’ll have a package stay at the “origin” process and then it randomly shows up. And their customer service is absolutely TERRIBLE. They refuse to answer any questions or take any accountability for anything, and if you sell, know you take all the risk if your buyer asks for a refund because their order never arrived. And that in itself is tricky because Collx tracking system is so iffy, the buyer could have gotten the cards and just not marked it as delivered because the tracking system will show the order as “cancelled postage” or still sitting at origin scan. Collx will give you vague and general responses when you bring this to their attention and offer no real assistance. Collx would be amazing if they would fix their tracking issues and take accountability and protect the seller just as much as they protect the buyer.

I've been a Pro member for about 4-5 yrs and have been through the ups & downs of this journey w/ CollX. To see where the app is now is  pretty amazing and as just a Pro subscriber, it feels incredible being a small part of that growth process. I'm not a seller and I use CollX app mainly to find the market value of cards and as a way to organize my collection digitally. Overall I'm thoroughly satisfied having my collection be in an orderly fashion from using the app. I've come to realize that finding the true value of cards is inherently difficult to determine. Idk the answer or if it's even possible to accurately find the true market value of a card with all the variables involved in such a complex process that is can be volatile at best with a target which is continuously moving and changing. That being said, the CollX app gives users/subscribers access to info that can help one come up with a more educated and accurate value of a card. However the info the app provides is only as good as the accuracy of that info. and imo, that is one thing CollX could improve upon, but I know how time consuming that is to stay current & up to date on. I do know CollX is constantly adding functions and improving upon some of its existing features & functionality which is a plus for all CollX users. I'd be remiss not to mention the CollX community and how the vast majority of members I've dealt with have been friendly, helpful, fair and honest. The same can be said for CollX support staff who generally have been pleasant to deal with and usually help solve or explain as best as possible any issues one may run into on the app. I have no problem telling all my friends and even strangers of the hobby about CollX and the benefits of being a Pro member for 4-5 yrs now. I will continue using app and letting others know about the CollX brand and how they have made the hobby better in a short period of time!

So I decided to set up shop, as it were, and list my collection on here for sale/trade. From the moment you create your shop, you’re peppered by “ambassadors” that try to build you up on the site’s perks and compete for your first sale. Once you actually sell a card to them, however, they vaporize from existence and will ignore you and any further message you send any of them. There’s clearly some kind of incentive for being a new user’s first buyer. Then you get into the meat of the app:
1) You are completely buried in advertisements to go Pro. They will literally pop every few listings and every single time you log on until you do. Just sign up for the free trial and cancel to get rid of most of them (although now they John’s users for their newest Pro tier).
2) The seller market is a ghost town. So many users aren’t active anymore, and the system still lets you make purchases from them. The issue? If you don’t file a return within 30 days, CollX keeps the money you spent on the card and you can’t get it back. Supposedly it’s paid to the seller, who isn’t active anyway so they won’t ever get it, but this is a mechanic that clearly needs to be changed.
3) You get a $10 store credit per month as a Pro member, so that easily explains why the ambassadors are willing to buy a cheap card from you. However, you can’t take the money out. Why? They require a $10 minimum transfer amount, AND they take $2 of it for every transfer as a fee. The $10 card I sold only paid me $7.20 after fees, and I can’t even remove it until someone buys something else. Even if I finally raise $10, I’ll only get $8, meaning I only made a paltry $5 of that first sale. I’m the months I’ve been on since, that remains the only sale.
CollX is nice if you want a catalogue of your cards and don’t mind relentless pop-up marketing to view it. Otherwise, leave it for the hardcore collectors that buy $100+ cards from each other and find a better place to sell your cards.

He asked for a refund I escalated it to support. They said to wait a little longer see if it showed. I reached out two times more times after that to support to get help. Never got any. At this point I moved on $20 whatever I stopped selling on this app. Then almost a whole year later they randomly let refund the buyer. So I reach out again asking about compensation. (Since most platforms will compensate both parties if you use their tracking and labels). Not with CollX first they told me there was no proof I sent the card…. I then supplied them with 8 screenshots of tracking scans messages etc…. Nope I don’t get compensated almost a year after all this because it doesn’t say it was delivered. So seller beware. This platform will NOT have your back under any circumstances.  I have deleted the app and will never use again.

Had some old sports cards I wanted to try selling. The scan feature is decent but on the majority of my scans, it scanned as the EU version and I had to manually switch it to the US version. 

I have sold a handful of $1-$5 cards, but with my experience selling trading cards, it’s very clear to me that a lot of sellers on this app are trying to confuse people and make them think something is more or less valuable than it actually is, especially trading cards like Pokémon and One Piece as the app does not pull data from TCGPlayer for market values.

Also, within my first few hours of downloading the app, I had several “CollX Ambassadors” reach out and offer me $10 for a card in my collection that I hadn’t even marked as for sale “wanting to be my first sale.” After thanking them for reaching out and offering some advice on how to set shipping options up in the app correctly, I realized I hadn’t fixed my card that was marked as the EU version which is worth a lot less than the US version that I have.

I have also had to report numerous “top sellers” for various scams such as messaging me to solicit various mystery packs that CollX does not allow to be sold on the app and marking bulk bin One Piece cards as “RARE!” 

TL;DR Good for selling a few sports cards here and there, very reasonable seller fees, but the scan tool isn’t very consistent, and a lot of the sellers have questionable ethics.

*Update: Developer reached out to provide a couple of tips on improving card scans and suggested Scan+. I did do a handful of card scans with Scan+, but still had some issues where it thought the card was the EU version, and therefore didn’t exactly feel like the Scan+ was worth the added fees.

That said, I have updated the review to 4-stars to better highlight the fact that it IS a good app—it’s just somewhat dragged down by the nature of a lot of sellers in the sports card market trying to make a profit by taking advantage of new users and people who don’t know the market very well.

From the few months I have used this app I have found it in general meeting my needs in cataloging my collection.
With that said there is definitely room for improvement. First and foremost identifying fake coins. I tested the app with a fake 1994 5oz China Panda silver plated. The coin app failed to recognize the obvious flaws in the fake ( eyes curve, the difference in the 1994 curvature, the different patterns in the tree background ext.
). That AI cannot be trusted to identify a fake so do not trust it.
Second is the lackluster updates to bullion coin value that still have not been adjusted. Almost all 2026 coinage has not been updated. It’s almost September so this should have been done get to work!
3rd
Grading is way off. The AI does not seem to be able to adjust or identify to toning in its algorithms and this can alter a coins value significantly.
Environmental damage causing a dark or uneven toning or even gunk on a coin does not seem to alter how the AI grades a coin.
I give this coin app a rating of 3 for the help it has given cataloging and ease of use for general purposes.

reviews.t: Only limited response from CoinSnap when asking for higher review of a coin submitted. Disappointing
reviews.b: I am writing to express my disappointment with both the accuracy of your app and the lack of meaningful customer support I have received.  I have submitted multiple requests regarding a Chinese gold coin that was incorrectly identified by the app. Despite taking the time to report these errors, I have not received an adequate response or seen any effort to correct my collection. As a result, the collection in my account no longer reflects the coins I actually own, making the app unreliable for inventory and record-keeping.  The value of a coin identification app depends on accurate identifications and responsive customer support. Unfortunately, my experience has been the opposite. Repeatedly reporting the same issues without resolution has been frustrating and has caused me to lose confidence in your service.  Because of this experience, I am canceling my subscription and request that my account and any inaccurate collection data associated with it be closed or deleted.

FoilSnap.title: TCG Card Scanner - FoilSnap
FoilSnap.desc:
Stop guessing. Start snapping. Whether you’re a dedicated Pokémon master, a seasoned Magic enthusiast, or a legendary Duelist, FoilSnap is the ultimate digital companion for your hobby. We’ve built the fastest, most accurate AI-powered scanner to help you identify cards, check market prices, and organize your collection in seconds.
FoilSnap turns your camera into a professional grading and valuation tool, ensuring you never miss the true price of a rare find.

KEY FEATURES:
Instant AI Scanning: Our advanced image recognition identifies cards instantly. Decode issuing game, year, card type, and backstory with a simple scan.
Precise Market Valuation: Stay ahead of the market. We pull live data from top marketplaces to give you the accurate card price for every scan.
Foil & Variant Detection: Unlike basic scanners, FoilSnap automatically detects if a card is a Foil or not, matching it to the correct premium price tier.
Multi-Genre Support: Manage your entire collection in one place. FoilSnap supports collectors of major TCGs like Magic, Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, and more.
Grading Assistant: Get a "pre-grade" estimate before you ship to PSA or BGS. Track centering, corners, and surface quality with our digital magnifying tool.
Portfolio Analytics: Watch your collection’s total price and value grow. 

Why Collectors Love FoilSnap
The "Foil" Advantage
Standard scanners often misidentify cards because of holographic glare. It distinguishes between a standard card and its holographic counterpart, ensuring the price you see reflects the actual card in your hand.
Price Tracking
Never leave money on the table at a trade. Instantly check the price of any card in your inventory. Whether you are buying, selling, or trading, you’ll have the up-to-date market price data at your fingertips.
Your Vault in Your Pocket
Never buy a duplicate by mistake again. Access your entire inventory at trade shows, local game stores, or while browsing the web. Save scans, monitor prices, and track your collection's growth.
FoilSnap provides price guide data and organization for fans of Magic: The Gathering (MTG), Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, MetaZoo!, and many other trading card and hobby franchises.

Upgrade to Premium for limitless identifications, exclusive market insights, and priority user support.

I downloaded this app to scan some sports cards, but it doesn’t work. It would misreport cards as being something else, or it wouldn’t be able to find the cards. I would upload screenshots for this review if I could. Then the app stopped working altogether and I did not get a response from Ludex support, so I cancelled my subscription and the app.  It was a waste of time and money and I’ll be looking elsewhere.

As a sports card collector, I’m always on the lookout for tools that make organizing, valuing, and selling my collection easier. Recently, I gave Ludex a try — a mobile app that promises card scanning, price tracking, and collection management. After spending time with it, here’s my full take.

⸻

📱 Native App Support

iPhone: Yes. Ludex runs natively on iPhone.
iPad: Technically yes… but not really. What you get is just the iPhone app scaled up to full screen. No iPad-specific interface, no extra features. Honestly, I would have preferred a fully functional web app where I could manage my collection from a desktop — but Ludex doesn’t offer that either.

⸻

⚡ Data Entry & Management
	•	Card Scanning: Functional, but slow. You can only scan one card at a time, and after each scan, you have to manually verify the card’s identification before moving on. Also, the app insists on playing an annoyingly loud camera shutter sound for every scan. If you’re scanning dozens of cards, prepare for your ears (and anyone nearby) to suffer.
	•	Database Search: Unknown. The app doesn’t make it clear how comprehensive its card database is.
	•	Import/Export: Nonexistent. If you were hoping to bulk-import your collection or export it for backup or selling, you’re out of luck.

⸻

🗂 Collection Management
	•	Custom Collections: Yes — Ludex calls these “custom binders.” They let you group similar cards together.
	•	Custom Tags or Metadata: No. You can’t add your own tags or custom fields to cards.
	•	Ease of Managing Custom Binders: This feature feels half-baked. To add a card to a custom binder, you first have to create the binder, open it, then manually add cards. Worse, you lose access to the powerful search filters available elsewhere in the app — no filtering by player, team, series, or listing status here.
The binder menu scrolls horizontally (why?!), there’s no way to sort binders, and binder names get cut off after ~15 characters on the main collections page. Not exactly collector-friendly.
	•	Once inside your collection, there’s no way to search for cards based on any information other than the player’s name. You have a ton of Topps Inception, you search “inception” and what do you get? Nothing. 

⸻

💰 Valuation & Marketplace Integration
	•	Real-Time Price Tracking: Yes. Prices update in real time, and the dashboard shows recent value changes in your collection.
	•	Multiple Price Sources: Yes — includes more than one data source for card values.
	•	Wishlists/Tradelists: No.
	•	Marketplace Access: No private marketplace, no Cardmarket or TCGPlayer integration. However, Ludex does have a built-in eBay integration for buying/selling.

⸻

👥 Community Features

There are none. No direct messages, no way to follow other collectors, no sharing collection stats inside the app.

⸻

🌐 Public Website for Sharing

Yes… but it’s a mess.

If you share a custom binder, the recipient can open it in their browser. On mobile, it’s passable. On desktop, it’s borderline comedy. The App Store and Google Play Store buttons are huge at the top — which makes no sense when someone’s already viewing on desktop. Below that is a QR code that’s literally four times larger than the card images. The actual cards — the whole reason the person clicked the link — are shoved to the bottom like an afterthought. Whoever designed this page needs to spend a week trying to share their own collection with it.

⸻

🔍 Search Functionality

The search feature across the app is extremely limited. You can search by player name and team — that’s it. No searching by card number, series, set, or any other metadata.

⸻

💵 Costs & Credits
	•	Annual Cost: $44.99
	•	Monthly Credit: $0.00

⸻

📝 Final Thoughts

Ludex has potential, but it’s frustratingly limited in too many areas. The card scanning works, but it’s slow and noisy. The collection management tools are basic and sometimes downright inconvenient. Marketplace integration is minimal, and the public web sharing feature — while technically there — feels more like a marketing push for the app than a genuine tool for collectors.

If you’re looking for an iPhone-only tool with basic scanning and real-time price updates, Ludex might fit your needs. But if you want a fast, flexible, and community-driven platform with robust search and sharing capabilities, you’ll likely be left wanting.

reviews.t: Great concept, issues make it a pain
reviews.b:
Hello, I want to preface this review by saying I love the concept and what was attempted with this app, and I enjoy how the devs have been responding to criticism and improving things. But this app is still full of issues, especially with Pokemon cards. The main issues I have encountered I will list below.

1. Pokemon card library. I do not know where Ludex gets its library of Pokemon cards, but it’s missing so much, some of the random promo cards and reprints is pretty excusable, but there’s some pretty well known cards that aren’t there

2. Search function. The search function if your card doesn’t scan correctly is a good concept but in execution this one is. completely broken, and I cannot find anything with it

3. Alternative versions of cards. If you have a version of a card that isn’t the main one from the packs or a reverse holo, you are out of luck. No option for metal variants, deck cards, or anything besides reverse holo is annoying, but it’s definitely not a HUGE issue

4. Binders. Binders are really hard to use, from someone trying to collect full sets. Good luck, if you want to use the broken search tool, you cannot search by set, also it’s found to be out of order from lack of a custom order option

Overall, I love this app, and I love the idea, but the issues are so jarring and make it almost impossible to collect the way the app intends you too. If these issues ever get fixed. Definitely a 5 star app.
Kobe Bryant R.I.P.

The best of PriceCharting and SportsCardsPro now on iOS! Find out what your collectibles are worth. Track market prices of video games, sports cards, Pokemon, YuGiOh, Magic the Gathering, Lorcana, and other trading cards, comic books, US coins, LEGO, and more. Completely free. We track thousands of sales from the top auction sites: eBay, Heritage, PWCC, and more, filter and sort them by condition into easy to use price guides.

PriceCharting allows you to:
- View pricing for all conditions of an item.
- View previous sales of collectibles from across the web. 
- Add items to your Collection to track their value over time. 
- Add items to your Wishlist  
- Use Search By Photo or Barcode Scanner to instantly ID your trading card or comic. 
- View all of the variations of your collectibles with our extensive photo catalog.
- Share collectibles with your friends via text message.
- Get notifications when items on your wishlist are listed below market value on eBay or our own marketplace
- Create lots from any number of items, add markups, and share PDF receipts when you're at conventions or just a garage sale
- Get grading recommendations for your ungraded collectibles that would gain the most value 

Example video games console supported: Playstation, PS2, PS3, PS4, PS5, Nintendo NES, SNES, Wii, Wii U, Gameboy, GBA, Nintendo DS , Xbox, Sega Genesis, Dreamcast,  and many others. 

Example Pokemon sets supported: Base Set, Scarlet & Violet, Pokemon 151, Vivid Voltage, Obsidian Flame, and every other Pokemon English and Japanese set.

IF you are just looking for a way to organize and track collections this app is fine but I wouldn’t rely on this app for prices that are consistently inline with their value. I’m not sure if they are using a terrible AI for data entry or people with extremely poor quality control issues. Either way the values entered aren’t always accurate.

Overall the app performs very well and has a great interface; easy to use, easy to organize, and basically glitch free since I’ve owned it; my only gripe is that the algorithm used to determine FMV of videogames is signicant flawed.  Since I’ve owned the app, I have found that on average their listed fmv’s across all games are at least 20% undervalued, and often times much more than that.  I’ve sold roughly 20 products in the last year and the closest projected value of all items sold was still 25% less that what I sold it for.  It’s not a dealbreaker and I prefer this to overvaluation however an important consideration.  I have not listed cards on here so perhaps these values are more accurate.  My advice would be to use multiple software tools at your disposal or just do the research yourself if you have the time.

reviews.t: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5 Stars: The Ultimate Pokémon Collection Tracker! Must Have for Every Trainer.
reviews.b:
If you’re collecting Pokémon cards, whether it’s Base Set classics, modern Scarlet & Violet pulls, Japanese sets, or chasing master sets, this app is a game changer. PriceCharting makes it ridiculously easy to scan cards with your phone camera, instantly see accurate values across conditions, like raw, PSA 10, CGC, etc., and track your entire collection’s worth in real time.
I love how it pulls from thousands of daily sales on eBay and top marketplaces, so you get reliable market data instead of guesswork. Add items in bulk, watch your portfolio grow, mark cards as sold to calculate real profits, and even browse population reports for rarity insights. It’s perfect for casual fans organizing binders or serious investors monitoring trends in sets like Pokémon 151, Vivid Voltage, or the latest drops. The interface is clean, scanning is fast and accurate for Pokémon TCG, plus other TCGs like Yu Gi Oh! and Magic, and the collection tools help you stay organized without the headache. No more wondering “what’s my collection worth?” Just open the app and see live totals, and with recent updates, they keep making it better, and the team clearly listens to feedback. Whether you’re building a competitive collection, flipping cards, or just nostalgic about your childhood favorites, PriceCharting turns your Pokémon hobby into something you can truly manage and enjoy. 

Download it now you’ll wonder how you ever collected without it! Highly recommended for every Pokémon fan. 🚀🔥 #PokemonTCG

reviews.t: PriceCharting is helpful for retro video game shopping!
reviews.b:
I use price charting solely for video game shopping. So I’m writing this from that perspective. Price charting helps me be a less naive shopper. It gives me the average cost of an item, which then I use that info to decide where/who I’ll buy from. Even if I’m not scoring always getting a discount, knowing I’m paying fair price makes me & my wallet feel better.

Sometimes though, the average price listed, is impossible to find, especially for less common games/cheap games. Also I don’t think it always accounts for shipping either in the average cost. However despite these things, I find it to be a helpful tool for video game shopping, to make sure you aren’t overpaying for things that are worth less than the listed price.

RareCandy.title: Rare Candy: TCG Card Scanner
RareCandy.desc:
Scan cards, track your collection, and open Instapacks to reveal real trading cards with Rare Candy.

SCAN YOUR CARDS
Identify raw and graded cards with your camera. Scan supported English and Japanese cards, check card details, and add your finds to your collection.

OPEN INSTAPACKS
Open curated digital packs and reveal real trading cards instantly. Keep your cards in your Vault, have them shipped to you, or exchange eligible cards for Candy credit. Explore available packs and find your next addition.

TRACK YOUR COLLECTION
Organize your cards in digital binders, follow master set progress, and manage your wishlist. Keep your collection updated as you scan.

SEE MARKET VALUES
Follow collection value and card-level price movement over time. Compare cards and use recent market data to inform your collecting decisions. Market values are estimates and vary with condition and available sales data.

COMPARE RAW AND GRADED VALUES
Grade Worthy compares raw and graded prices to help you prioritize cards for potential grading. It is a price comparison tool, not a guarantee of a card's grade or future value.

SHOP VERIFIED LISTINGS
Browse verified sellers, singles, sealed products, auctions, pre-orders, and new drops.

JOIN THE COMMUNITY
Share binders, show off your pulls, follow creators, and see what other collectors are building.
Create an account to get started. Instapacks and marketplace purchases are paid.

As a lifelong Pokémon lover, opening packs has always been about more than just the cards. It’s about the excitement, the nostalgia, the anticipation, and the love for something that has brought joy to so many of us over the years. That’s why I decided to give Rare Candy a chance.

Unfortunately, my experience has been extremely disappointing. Pack after pack, I’ve found myself feeling frustrated, let down, and honestly, almost scammed. I understand that opening Pokémon packs comes with no guarantees, and I don’t expect to pull a rare or valuable card every time. That’s part of the hobby. But there’s a difference between accepting the luck of the draw and feeling like the entire experience is designed to leave you disappointed.

The saddest part of this experience is that it’s starting to take away my love for Pokémon. Something that has brought me happiness for years is now associated with frustration and distrust because of an app that I chose to give a chance.

No company should make a genuine fan feel this way about something they love. Pokémon has always been about the excitement of opening a pack and the memories that come with it. I never thought an app would make me question that love.

I’m sharing this because I genuinely care about Pokémon, and I wish my experience with Rare Candy had been different. I wanted to enjoy the experience, support the hobby, and have fun opening packs. Instead, I’ve been left disappointed and questioning whether it’s even worth continuing.

It takes a lot for something you’ve loved for years to start losing its magic. I hope Rare Candy takes feedback like this seriously, because behind every purchase is a real person, a real fan, and someone who simply wants to enjoy the hobby they love.

reviews.t: Fast, useful, and actually makes scanning cards easier
reviews.b:
I’ve only recently started using Rare Candy seriously, but I’m already impressed with the scanner. The auto-scan feature is very fast, and even with less-than-ideal lighting it identified most of my Pokémon cards correctly. I also like that it keeps a recent-scan session together so I can go back and verify everything afterward instead of stopping after every card.

It isn’t perfect — I had a few misidentifications when I left it on “Any Card” in poor lighting, so some of that may have been my setup rather than the app itself. I also occasionally had to correct a variant, but that was easy to fix.

The important part is that Rare Candy does most of the hard work for me and makes inventorying a large collection feel much more manageable. I had been putting off scanning my cards because I expected it to be tedious, but after using Rare Candy with a scan station, I realized this could actually become a workflow I’ll use regularly.

I’ve really enjoyed using the Rare Candy app. When it’s working properly, it’s a great way to organize and track my collection, and the scanning feature is a huge time-saver.

That said, there are a few improvements I’d love to see:

* Add the ability to sort binders by card number and rarity. This would make organizing collections much easier.
* Sometimes after scanning a card, it won’t let me add it to my collection right away. I have to completely close and reopen the app before it works again.
* It would be awesome if binders could have custom cover photos instead of being limited to solid colors. That would make collections feel much more personal and easier to identify at a glance.

Overall, it’s a great app with a lot of potential. Fixing these issues and adding these quality-of-life features would easily make it a 5-star experience.

- The current interface is visually appealing, but each line item on a scan-list or collection takes up a relatively huge amount of space on screen, with no way to compact it.

- Lastly, searching individual cards in the scan tab makes no attempt to search by best match. Searching for the yugioh card “Witch of the White Forest” returns nearly a thousand results, beginning with MTG *spindown dice*.

RockIdentifier.desc:
Rock Identifier is an all-in-one stone, crystal, mineral, and gemstone identifier. Simply take or upload a photo of a rock or crystal, and the app will tell you all about it in seconds. 

Want to know the name of a stone you discovered in your rock hounding? Are you curious about the different properties of each stone and crystal you own? Looking to learn about rock and crystal knowledge? Don't miss this powerful stone identifier and crystal guidebook. We will satisfy all your needs!

Rock & Mineral & Crystal Identifier
Take a photo of any crystals or gemstones and get an instant accurate identification. This rock scanner app can recognize over 6,000 types of rocks and minerals and helps anyone who wants to identify, examine and explore the characteristics of stones.

Stone & Crystal Encyclopedia
In each of the identification results, the Rock Identifier app provides detailed stone/crystal information which includes: Name, Chemical Formula, Hardness, Colour Variations, and the main locations it can be found. 
No matter whether you are a beginner rock hound who is trying to identify the stones you discovered or an experienced crystal collector who wants to expand your geological knowledge, Rock Identifier offers the easiest and most comprehensive rock guide.

Real VS Fake Gemstone
This app delivers detailed and practical gemstone identification method articles, where users can learn to identify if a gemstone or crystal is real by its Color, Cleavage and Fracture, Touch, Shape, Transparency, and the like. 

Explore Trendy Stones
Interested in the healing properties of any crystals? Want to know what gemstones to have for your specific zodiac sign? Download this rock scanner app to find out the mysterious healing power of crystals, and learn more facts about zodiac stones, birthstones, and so much more.

Metal Detector
Lost your key and have no idea how to find it? With the in-app Metal Detector function, Rock Identifier can help you locate your lost key by measuring the surrounding magnetic field strength. Never worry about losing metal objects again!

One-on-one Consultation with Rock Expert
This scanner app not only provides you with lively, professional knowledge of mineralogy and petrology but also offers an email service for one-on-one inquiry help.

Unique Rock Collections
Display all your stone and mineral collectibles with the Collection function; add desirable crystals and gemstones to your wishlist. The app will also automatically keep your ID record so that you can go back to find them.

Rock Identifier was created to help more people explore and learn about the geological surroundings around them.
Download the app today to enjoy a more pleasant stone & crystal journey and train yourself to be a rock expert!

I’m a collector of crystals, so an app that allows you to simply photograph a stone & then identifies it for you is like a dream come true. While there is definitely room for improvement, it seems the developers of the app are well aware of this, encouraging the user to participate in this process, which I appreciate. I’d love to see a few things, such as: 1) the ability to print out ones rock /crystal collection, (ie I have 70 stones in my collection in the app, so a visual color chart that allows one to include your original photos and the name & main properties of each rock) I think would be super exciting, instead of just downloading other people’s charts of “the most important stones” since this is ultimately subjective and could be very creative. 2) the ability to add text to one’s personal collection. For instance, if I could, I’d write my own metaphysical associations and/or properties of the stones, & how I use the stone in my own life/work. While there is currently a plethora of source material in this realm, to combine the ability to identify & create one’s own personal, experiential source material via photograph and then recorded uses, metaphysical properties etc. would make this app an essential tool in one’s own process of discovery and learning.

HoloDex.title: HoloDex - TCG Scan & Collect
HoloDex.desc:
HoloDex is the fastest way to scan, grade, and organize your trading card collection. Whether you're managing a childhood binder or flipping alt arts from the latest set, HoloDex gives you real-time prices, powerful organization tools, AI grading insights, and instant card recognition, all from your phone.

Now supporting more TCGs than ever: Pokémon TCG, One Piece Card Game, Disney Lorcana TCG, Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG, Magic: The Gathering, Dragon Ball Super Card Game, Digimon Card Game, Gundam Card Game, Union Arena, Riftbound, and Star Wars: Unlimited.

Instant Card Scanning
Just point your camera and scan. Identify cards in seconds across supported games, from Pokémon Base Set to Scarlet & Violet, to the latest MTG, One Piece, Lorcana, and Yu-Gi-Oh! releases.

AI Grading
Get instant condition analysis using AI. Spot whitening, centering issues, and surface wear before you grade, trade, or sell.

Real-Time Card Values
Check live market prices instantly so you always know what your cards are worth.

Organize Your Collection
Build portfolios, track duplicates, and create wishlists. Your digital collection stays synced and accessible anywhere.

Secure Cloud Backup
Your collection is safe and available across all devices. Never lose track of a card again.

Whether you're a casual fan or serious collector, HoloDex helps you stay organized, protect value, and make smarter trading decisions, across all your favorite TCGs.

Key Features

- Multi-TCG support: Pokémon, One Piece, Lorcana, Yu-Gi-Oh!, and Magic: The Gathering
- AI card scanner with instant recognition
- AI grading insights for card condition
- Real-time market price tracking
- Portfolio and collection management
- Wishlist tracking
- Multi-device sync
- Multi-currency support
- Track profits and losses

- Unlimited card scans
- Exclusive filters
- AI Grading

reviews.t: AI Grade Doesn’t Match the Condition Description
reviews.b:
I really like the idea behind HoloDex’s AI grading, and the interface is clean and easy to use. However, my recent grading report exposed a major inconsistency that makes me question the reliability of the results.

My card received an overall AI grade of 6.4, but the app labeled it as “Excellent–Near Mint.” The detailed analysis then described:

* Edges (4): Severe whitening and chipping along the back.
* Corners (5): Significant whitening and wear on all four corners.
* Surface (6): Multiple scratches, scuffing, and staining.
* Centering (9): Good centering.

The summary even states the card shows heavy signs of play and wear and that the edge and corner damage significantly lowered the grade.

Those descriptions clearly do not match a condition labeled “Excellent–Near Mint.” A 6.4 and comments describing severe wear should not be presented alongside a Near Mint condition.

I’m not upset about receiving a 6.4 if that’s what the AI believes the card deserves. My concern is that the condition label contradicts both the numerical grade and the written analysis. If new collectors rely on these labels, they could easily misunderstand the true condition of their cards.

I hope the developers review the grading scale or fix this apparent bug because the AI analysis itself has potential. Consistency between the grade, condition label, and written report is essential if users are going to trust the app.

reviews.t: Great app - but clearly needs more time to develop
reviews.b:
I just recently downloaded HoloDex and I am enjoying how easy the app is to use. The scan feature to find cards and the ability to add any condition/grade to a card is something that sets it apart from a lot of other apps. 

A few negatives however: 

I purchased HoloDex pro, and no matter how hard I try, the highest the AI grader gave my card was a 9.4 (funny because it is slabbed as a PSA 10). The grader needs some sort of key. 
For instance: If the grader gives  ~9, then psa would likely give a 10. And if the grader gives a perfect 10, then theoretically the card should be a BGS black label. We need some way of understanding how the AI grader translates into actual grades for each company. 

Another negative: I spoke about how great it is that you can add grades for your cards, and how you can also add conditions. The issue with this however, is the app’s database does not have prices for certain grades or cards. So all of the LP cards in my portfolio have TBD as their price. Also, for PSA 10 cards with low population, the price I put I paid for the card ended up being the market price on the app, not the real market price.

Overall, HoloDex is an app with great potential, but it needs to update its databases and give clarity as to what its grades mean. If the developers care about the future of their app and keep updating it and its database, I don’t doubt that it can become one of the best card scanning and grading apps.

reviews.t: Inconsistent AI grading and not free to try out.
reviews.b: Wanted to try this “AI Grading” everyone is talking about online and saw this app advertised on a YouTube video. Not very impressed. The AI Grading in this app was not free to try and required you to sign up for a monthly or annual membership. I chose just the monthly membership for $7.99 to try out the software. I have a Mega Charizard X EX #125 SIR from Phantasmal Flames I want to get graded. After using the AI grading App twice on the same card, it gave 2 different grades (first one an 8.5 and the second one a 9) with completely different reasoning for both grade reports. Pictures were taken on the same dark colored background using natural light. The grade reports gave different information for the rear centering and the rear edges of the card. One grade report said the edges showed whitening on the top edge whereas the other grade report said it was very sharp and clean. One grade report said that the rear centering was off center to the top and right and the other grade report said the rear centering was off center to the bottom and right. Even when you measure the rear centering with an actual centering tool it is within the 55/45 split specification but the AI Grading report rated it an 8.5. Will not continue the membership and highly discourage people from wasting their money on this gimmick of an app.

I’m sure the app is great, but I am not coming back for the prices. Hate it when card service apps do this. We should be paying little to nothing, if anything at all. Would recommend PriceCharting and TCGplayer for card tracking, and Card Grader Pro for AI grading. They at least let you use the app, and the main features of the app is free. They make you pay extra for special features, not to use the app at all. Hate this.

Dragon Shield's PokeTCG app has completely transformed the way I manage my trading card game (TCG) collection. As an avid Pokémon TCG collector, I've tried various inventory apps, and this one stands out as a true gem.
The feature that truly sets this app apart is its seamless digital inventory system. Adding cards to your collection is a breeze, thanks to the intuitive interface and the ability to quickly scan cards using your device's camera. The accuracy of the scans is impressive, with very few misreads. It's a time-saver for anyone looking to catalog their collection efficiently.

One of the standout features for me is the app's ability to provide instant card values. This is a game-changer for collectors who want to stay updated on the market. The pricing information is regularly updated, ensuring that you have the most accurate and current values for your cards. Whether you're looking to buy, sell, or simply keep track of your collection's overall worth, this feature is invaluable.

The user interface is clean, visually appealing, and user-friendly. Navigating through your collection is a breeze, and the app's organization tools make it easy to find specific cards or filter your collection based on various criteria. The addition of customizable tags and notes further enhances the organizational capabilities, allowing users to personalize their experience.

The app also provides a robust set of features for managing duplicates and trades. You can easily track multiple copies of a card, and the trade functionality makes it simple to keep tabs on your ongoing trades and potential swaps with other collectors.

In terms of performance, the app runs smoothly and responds quickly. Updates are frequent, addressing any bugs or issues promptly. The developers seem genuinely committed to improving and refining the user experience, which is always a positive sign for the longevity of an app.

Overall, Dragon Shield's PokeTCG app is a must-have for any trading card game enthusiast. It combines a user-friendly interface, accurate scanning capabilities, real-time card values, and comprehensive collection management tools. Whether you're a seasoned collector or just starting your TCG journey, this app is an invaluable companion that will undoubtedly enhance your collecting experience. Highly recommended!

reviews.t: Forget it if you collect Japanese/rare cards
reviews.b:
I was honestly pretty excited to find this app, as the premise sounded great and was exactly what I was looking for in app form (keep tabs of my collection, prices, etc…)
Unfortunately, the app barely met my expectations on a few fronts which I will list below.
1. The scan tool is REALLY hit or miss, especially when it comes to full art cards. If you’re thinking you’ll be able to simply scan all of your cards and add them to your virtual collection, don’t. Some cards do scan almost instaneously, but they are far and few between. Normally they either 1. Don’t scan at all, despite changing the light, angle, distance, etc… 2. Will miscan a card as another (for example my giratina alt art lost origins card kept getting scanned as an unknown card) 
2. Forget it if you collect Japanese cards. A lot of rare Japanese cards that I have aren’t even in the database when you search for them (ie my Charizard EX 276 XY promo card). Switching the card to a different language also doesn’t do anything at all (doesn’t change to a photo representing the card in that language, and more importantly, the non-English/American prices). 
3. The search tool is way too finicky, and will leave you guessing what a card has been entered as in their database. 
4. The prices honestly don’t seem that accurate. I have sold cards easily for more than prices listed, and definitely bought cards for less than prices listed (without having to try hard at all).
5. The overall layout of the app is a little cluttered, and requires one too many steps to add a card, making adding cards a chore instead of a breeze. 

I figured I would give the free premium trial a run, and was honestly planning on paying the very reasonable $3 a month afterwards, but I now will probably delete the app as a whole, and just stick to adding cards to my TCGplayer account. Again, just wanted an app on my phone that would allow me to remember what cards I have (especially while visiting shops during my travels to Japan), but this app definitely isn’t it. 
If you have a barebones and basic collection, I’m sure it works wonders. Unfortunately, if you have any card a little “out of the norm” (and usually pretty expensive), this app definitely won’t allow you to keep an accurate track of your collection, which is a shame.

A great app for tracking both collections and decks. The ability to categorize and sort between specific releases of cards is incredibly handy, and the price updates are great as well. The even trade function has served me well at my LGS and for trading with friends. 

I do wish there was a way to share the Wishlist or export it to a TCGPlayer cart. IMO as someone looking to complete a few collections that’s one of the biggest things the app is missing.

App Design:
There are aspects of this application that do not really conform to iOS application design patterns a and it feels cumbersome to understand for users familiar with the platform. 

Swipe shortcuts could be more intuitive, the bottom sticking bar also feels foreign. 

Scanning cards had the tendency to misidentify which set some of my older cards were from and the set-selection picker did not contain the correct set. 

I noticed that “first edition” is not an option for older cards. This made it tricky for me to categorize cards that were both foil AND first edition. 

The free mode is pretty generous so thank you for that.

reviews.t: Card pricing impossible to keep accurate
reviews.b:
I’ve scanned about 500 cards as a part of a folder in my inventory on the app. When you add the cards, it will tell you the market price for the card. This is nice, but what fails to be made clear is you should actually add the “price you paid” for the card, since it seems to value the market price vs what you got it for. Then it shows a + or - based on how much money the card is worth. 

After a bug in the app, all my card values crashed about 50% (this was when cards were being shown incorrectly bug), but now with the cards back to expected, all the prices are all out of whack, so now my 500ish card collection says I’ve lost about half my worth. But it’s wrong. So that’s annoying. 

DEVELOPERS: It would be nice if there were a way to reset card values, or reset all of a selected folders card values to their current market price.

reviews.t: Amazing App, Nothing Else To Say
reviews.b: This app is flat out amazing, and it has so many features to boot! It has the inventory feature, which is really cool because you can add folders and the colors are extra vivid. Seriously, you have to see how Charizard would look! Creating decks is so awesome, because most scan apps like this would stop at an inventory and scanner. But no! You can even simulate your decks while you’re at it! Again, the graphics are amazing. A wishlist is available, too? Oh my god. I can put ANY card I want there and that is what I have been doing. There is even a sold option which I am excited to see come. The extra features such as the winners and losers are nice, and the scanner is really good and it doesn’t scan everything while still being quite ok. And did I mention, creating an account unlocks all these features while being free! Most apps are, create your account for $9.99 a month! It’s trash. But this app fixes that!And that’s all I have to say for right now, and I would totally recommend this for beginners and I’m only 2 days in!

More people need to download this app. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve seen folks ask online how much a single card is worth. Whereas I have to value over 100s of cards in a single day! So of course, I needed something to make my life easier. And this app is so quick and easy to use, and I’ve rarely encountered issues with it. Of course, the scanner isn’t perfect but I noticed it’s getting much better with each release. 

And the few times I have noticed some bugs myself, I emailed their support team and they were super responsive and quick to jump on fixing the issues. I even suggested some new features and enhancements, which they said they liked and I appreciate the acknowledgment at least. You just don’t see that kind of support from other apps. (And as a Product Manager for several small websites & mobile apps, I can tell you now that this is not the norm. Most of those support emails get auto-generated into a ticket and just sit in a backlog somewhere to grow old and die lol.)

Anyways, I highly recommend any hardcore Pokémon card collector like myself to use this app. It’ll save you so much time keeping track of your inventory and pricing. I personally collect Pokémon cards to complete master sets. And it’s hard to keep track of what you own (I have over 1000 cards atm). Quick, easy way to keep inventory of your collection and sort cards digitally instead of handling them(if you’re a collector) and manage deck arrangements (if you’re a player). 

Perks - Easy to use interface.
- Extremely helpful tool that is rare among free apps that focus on media giants. I’ve only used the free version and haven’t felt limited by paywalls, the premium version seems to offer better insight into the market if you’re serious about trading.

Cons - Scanner can be very sensitive and assume almost anything is artwork, like it assumes my blue jeans are a machoke or my couch cushion is a suicune between scanning cards.
- scans can also be less than accurate, which can be corrected via manual data entry, which again is very easy because the ui is beautifully simplistic. It’s not really an app-breaking problem, but it does make the process take a bit longer due to manually ensuring the card is catalogued correctly.  A button to trigger the scan feature would be great, in lieu of the scan being triggered automatically upon ‘recognizing’ the card upon entering the frame.

TL;DR great app for what it is, no forced paywall features that hobble the app.

reviews.t: Decent, but has a ways to go
reviews.b:
I’m a big fan of Dragon Shield’s card protectors, so I was curious when I saw this app in the AppStore. I’ve been looking for apps to catalogue my collection, and this app’s features like using the camera to scan in cards, pulling in pricing data, and future promised features made me want to give it a try. 

First, I noticed cards from newer sets like Battle Styles weren’t scanning in, but older sets like base and Jungle scanned in quickly with no issue. If the card doesn’t scan in you can do a search for the card via text entry, but the way this app presents multiple cards for a particular Pokemon are extremely confusing and you have to check through each result individually to match up the correct card. Even some cards that did manage to scan in would indicate the wrong set since the same card appeared in multiple sets. 

The subscription tiers are reasonably priced at face value, but when you look at how nearly every premium feature is “coming soon” it’s actually a bit expensive at this stage where you’re just paying for card slots. 

I do appreciate the ability to set the quantity I have of a specific card and get pricing data at a glance. This product just seems like it was released in Beta and there’s still a lot of bugs to work out. No excuse to have cards missing when that data is so easy to obtain.
